arguments.question: what arguments does executeTool need?
arguments.statement: One required argument, and it must be a Tool: the browser says so twice. The method declares an arity of 1 (Function.length of a native method is its required-argument count), and a call with nothing at all answers a Promise rejected as TypeError: Failed to execute 'executeTool' on 'ModelContext': 1 argument required, but only 0 present. Passing undefined, a descriptor-shaped plain object, a name string, or an object carrying only a name each answers a Promise rejected as TypeError: Failed to execute 'executeTool' on 'ModelContext': parameter 1 is not of type 'Tool'. The tree’s prose gives the call as executeTool(tool, args, { signal }) — three arguments — but the input object and the signal are optional in this binding: the first argument’s type is rejected before they can matter, and no call measured here ever reached them.
arguments.handleArgumentBasis: the WebIDL refusal text names the interface ("parameter 1 is not of type 'Tool'"), and the same interface is a global whose prototype lists name, description, title, window, origin, inputSchema, outputSchema and annotations

static.statement: The prototype record says executeTool is a member of document.modelContext’s prototype, the tree’s prose gives it the signature executeTool(tool, args, { signal }) and executeTool(tool, input, {signal}), and `tool` is a descriptor from the array getTools() answers. No line in this tree records a call, so the arity above is the browser’s answer and not the tree’s.

citations.lineText: - **WebMCP is live in both browsers:** `typeof document.modelContext === 'object'` (`navigator.modelContext` is `undefined`). The prototype has `registerTool`, `getTools`, `executeTool`, `ontoolchange`, `ontoolactivated` and `ontoolcancel`.

- [measured, W1] **Agent-side API (what an extension needs):** `document.modelContext.getTools({ fromOrigins })` -> array of `{ name, description, inputSchema, origin, window }`; `document.modelContext.executeTool(tool, args, { signal })` runs the tool in the owner's context; `toolchange` event when tools are added/removed.

- The API is `document.modelContext` with `registerTool`, `getTools({fromOrigins})` and `executeTool(tool, input, {signal})`, plus `toolchange`, `toolactivated` and `toolcancel` events; `executeTool` resolves to the JSON-stringified return value of `execute`, whatever its shape, so the MCP `{content: [...]}` array is a convention, not a rule **[measured, `index.bs`]**. 00 measured the same members on `document.modelContext` in both browsers.

answerShape.question: what does executeTool answer, and through which shape?
answerShape.statement: A Promise — including when the call is wrong. No call measured here threw synchronously: each returned a thenable object whose constructor is Promise and reported its refusal as a rejection of that promise, so a caller that does not await gets an unhandled rejection and never an exception at the call site. No call resolved: every answer recorded here is a rejection, and each is a TypeError raised by the binding before the tool could run. What a successful call resolves to is therefore unobserved here; the tree’s documented answer — the JSON-stringified return value of the tool’s execute, whatever its shape — is a citation, not an observation.
answerShape.refusalShape: a rejected promise carrying a TypeError (constructor TypeError, name TypeError, no DOMException code)

static.statement: The tree records the success shape twice: executeTool(tool, args, { signal }) "runs the tool in the owner’s context", and the spec reading says executeTool resolves to the JSON-stringified return value of execute, whatever its shape, so an MCP-shaped { content: [...] } result is a convention rather than a rule.

noModel.question: what does executeTool answer where no model is available?
noModel.statement: Not observed, and this recording will not state it as if it were: no launch produced a page with the surface present and the model unavailable. The instance’s on-device model is installed and LanguageModel.availability() answered "available" in both launches, and nothing this task may do — clearing a multi-gigabyte model another session shares, or inventing an answer — can produce the missing state. What the two launches did establish is that the model and the surface are separate facts, which is what SC2 needs in order to render no-model distinctly from unavailable.
noModel.why: the model is a disk component of the shared chrome-beta-nano profile, LanguageModel.availability() reads it, and this task neither clears it nor starts an instance without it. The --no-ai-features launch removes the feature switches, not the model: it answers the surface question, not the model question.

observedInstead.statement: Two facts were measured, and neither is a no-model answer for executeTool. (a) With the registry features on, a model was available (LanguageModel.availability() answered "available") and executeTool’s refusal named the type of its first argument, never a model; the method’s own source is [native code] and the string "model" appears in it only as part of the interface’s name. (b) With --no-ai-features, document.modelContext was undefined — the surface was absent, so there was no method to answer with — while LanguageModel was still present and still answered "available". So a missing model is not what makes executeTool refuse and a missing surface is what makes it unreachable: on this API the model is needed to choose a tool, not to invoke one.

static.statement: No line in this tree ties executeTool to a model: the prose describes it as running the tool in the owner’s context and resolving to the tool’s own return value, and the model appears only as the agent that chooses which tool to call.

invocation.question: can a tool be invoked at all on a page that declares none?
invocation.statement: No. The one required argument is a Tool the browser owns, and this page owns none: its own awaited getTools() resolved to [], so getTools()[0] is undefined and executeTool(undefined, {}, {}) answers a Promise rejected as TypeError: Failed to execute 'executeTool' on 'ModelContext': parameter 1 is not of type 'Tool'. A caller cannot make the handle itself either: Tool is a global interface whose constructor is illegal — new Tool() throws TypeError: Failed to construct 'Tool': Illegal constructor — so a descriptor-shaped object, a name string and a new Tool() are all refused identically, as parameter 1 not being of type Tool. Tool.prototype carries name, description, title, window, origin, inputSchema, outputSchema and annotations: a Tool exists only as a value the browser produced, and registerTool is the only way this tree records for a page to put one there — which prohibition N4 forbids this milestone from using to make an invocation observable.
refusals: TypeError: Failed to execute 'executeTool' on 'ModelContext': parameter 1 is not of type 'Tool'.
TypeError: Failed to construct 'Tool': Illegal constructor

static.statement: The tree records both halves of this: a tool comes into existence through registerTool({ name, description, inputSchema, execute }, { signal, exposedTo }), and the tool list is read through getTools({ fromOrigins }), whose array of { name, description, inputSchema, origin, window } is where a descriptor comes from. Nothing in the tree records a call of either.

controls.question: is the surface this recording measured the one the instance reports after the no-features launch was closed?
controls.what: The no-features launch was closed and the instance restarted with its registry switches; the expression that opened the measurement was then run again unchanged. It answered the same shape: document.modelContext an object, executeTool a native function of arity 1 on the prototype, and the same seven prototype members. This is a control, not an answer to the question — it says the registry launch whose answers are recorded above is the launch the instance reports by default.

answer.statement: On chrome-beta-nano, Chrome/159.0.8154.13, and https://example.com/: document.modelContext.executeTool is a native data property of ModelContext.prototype with an arity of 1; it always answers a Promise and refuses with a TypeError, never throwing at the call site. What it needs is one argument of type Tool — not a model, and not an arguments object, which no measured call ever reached — and where the page declares no tool there is no such Tool: getTools() resolved to [], and Tool is a global interface with an illegal constructor, so a caller cannot fabricate the handle either. So on the measured API a tool cannot be invoked at all on a page that declares none: the answer is a rejection naming its argument’s type, and that refusal is the state SC2 must render rather than a result.
answer.needs: one argument of type Tool: a handle the browser produced
answer.doesItNeedAModelBasis: no measured answer mentions a model, the method’s source names none, and the one launch that removed the AI features still reported the model as available while removing the surface — so the model is needed to choose a tool, not to call one
answer.answers: a Promise in every case measured: rejections carrying TypeError text from the binding; no synchronous throw, and no resolved value observed
answer.whereNoModelIsAvailable: unobserved, and recorded as unobserved: the model was available in both launches, and the state that could be produced instead (features off) removes the surface rather than the model
answer.effectOnTheMilestone: SC2’s refusal states are the reachable ones on this page, and the surface must carry the API’s own refusal text as its reason with no result beside it; a rehearsal needs a page that declares a tool before any invocation can succeed, which is Wave 2’s and Wave 3’s problem and not this recording’s claim.

notClaimed: Nothing here claims what executeTool answers when it succeeds: no page that declares a tool was measured, so no Tool handle ever existed, every measured call was refused before the tool could run, and the documented resolution (the JSON-stringified return value of the tool’s execute, research/14-ai-devtools-prior-art.md:327) is a citation rather than an observation here.

Nothing here registers a tool to make an invocation observable: the fabricated descriptors in the live expressions were passed as arguments and never handed to registerTool, so no observation in this recording depends on a registration, and none can say what the API does for a tool a page really owns.

Nothing here claims a second browser, channel, version or page: one instance (chrome-beta-nano, Chrome/159.0.8154.13) and one page (https://example.com/) were measured, and the two other launches recorded above are the same instance on the same version with different feature switches.

Nothing here claims what executeTool answers where no model is available: the instance’s on-device model is installed and LanguageModel.availability() answered "available" in both launches, so `measurement.noModel.observedHere` is false and the state is named as unobserved rather than inferred. The launch without the AI feature switches removes the surface, not the model, and left the model reporting available.

Nothing here claims user activation, the `tools` permissions policy or an origin-exposure rule changes the answer: navigator.userActivation.isActive read true in every expression, so a page without activation was never among the measured states.

Nothing here claims the recording is complete for the API: the seven prototype members printed, the eight Tool.prototype member names read, and the two DOMException-free TypeErrors recorded are what this one instance and version answered, and no other member, event or argument was exercised.

Nothing here renders, registers or relays: no caller, no join, no panel surface and no route was written by this task, and the extension build that ran before the measurement only produced the panel bundle the instance loads.

citations.lineText: "note": "there is no `.d.ts`, no ambient declaration and no interface for `modelContext` in the tree. The two probe lines are `modelContext: typeof navigator.modelContext` (spikes/probes/probe3.js:5 and spikes/probes/probe4.js:5), the superseded spelling."
